title: Drowning
summary: Rescue without entering the water if you can. For a drowned person who is not breathing, breaths are especially important: give rescue breaths and start CPR.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for every drowning incident
when: Anyone pulled from the water who is unresponsive, not breathing normally, coughing persistently or confused
Anyone who needed rescue breaths or CPR, even if they recover

steps.title: Stay safe – reach, throw, don't go
steps.text: Do not enter the water unless trained and equipped. Reach with a pole or branch, or throw a buoyant object or rope. Floodwater and moving water are extremely dangerous.

steps.title: Check breathing
steps.text: Once on dry land, check response and open the airway and check for normal breathing.

steps.title: Give rescue breaths
steps.text: If not breathing normally, give 5 initial rescue breaths if trained (ERC), then start CPR at 30 compressions to 2 breaths.
steps.caution: Drowning is a lack of oxygen – rescue breaths matter. If you cannot give breaths, do compressions only.

steps.title: Start CPR and use an AED
steps.text: Dry the chest before attaching AED pads.

steps.title: If breathing
steps.text: Place in the recovery position, keep warm, and watch closely – people who have nearly drowned can deteriorate later.

doNot: Do not enter the water yourself unless trained
Do not try to drain water from the lungs or use abdominal thrusts
Do not let them go home without medical assessment

sources.title: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
